capabilities.target: chat transcript returned to the authenticated requester
arbitrary external URL chosen by the model at call time

inputs.source: Employee question via SSO-authenticated chat client
Engineering design docs retrieved via docs.search
Jira tickets filed by customers, via planned Jira MCP server integration

instructions.note: The prompt instructs the agent to answer engineering questions for any authenticated requester with no stated audience restriction. Runtime notes restrict write access to the design docs to engineers but say nothing about who may query them, so any authenticated employee, regardless of role, can extract confidential engineering content through natural-language questions.

The only control against leaking secrets or credentials that might appear in the design docs is a model-obeyed instruction ('Never paste secrets or credentials into answers'). This is a dependent, behavioral control that decays under model_upgrade and longer_task_horizon, and it only addresses secrets specifically, not general confidential disclosure.

elements.name: Arbitrary external URL reachable via planned web.fetch

controls.name: Reply destination bound to the authenticated requester
controls.decay_rationale: The chat client always returns the answer to the same authenticated session that asked the question, and renders no images and fetches no links, closing common side-channel egress. The destination comes from the system of record (the session), not from model output, so this does not decay with model capability.

controls.name: Read-only credential for docs.search
controls.decay_rationale: The credential used by docs.search cannot write or delete. This does not decay with model capability, though it could be widened under data_scope_expansion.

controls.name: Only docs.search and chat reply are wired into the agent today
controls.decay_rationale: No egress-capable tool such as web.fetch exists today, so the model currently has no channel to reach an attacker-controlled destination beyond the bound chat reply. This is effectively a tool allowlist, which fails under new_tool and new_mcp_server because those triggers are defined as adding exactly the tool or server this control's protection depends on not existing.

controls.name: Prompt instruction: never paste secrets or credentials into answers
controls.decay_rationale: Relies on the model choosing to comply and only addresses secrets/credentials specifically, not general confidential content. Fails under model_upgrade and longer_task_horizon.

controls.name: Only engineers can write to the design docs store
controls.decay_rationale: Enforced by write permissions outside the model; does not decay with model capability. Protects document integrity (relevant to future memory/content poisoning) but does not restrict who may read or query the docs.

controls.name: Role-based restriction on who may query confidential design docs
controls.decay_rationale: Not present in the design. SSO authentication confirms identity, not entitlement to confidential engineering content.

controls.name: Network egress allowlist restricting web.fetch destinations
controls.decay_rationale: Not present in the design. If added and scoped to destinations an attacker cannot write to or register, this would sever the exfiltration path rather than merely narrow it.

controls.name: Provenance isolation for Jira ticket content
controls.decay_rationale: Not present in the design. Would tag customer-filed ticket content as untrusted and prevent it from directly shaping tool call arguments without review; a stronger model can still route around content tagging it does not enforce itself.

controls.name: Raw-action human approval gate on web.fetch
controls.decay_rationale: Not present in the design. A raw-action gate showing the full destination URL and parameters would hold the residual floor at moderate even without severing the path outright.

findings.title: Confidential design docs answered for any authenticated employee, not limited to engineering

attack_path.note: Confidential engineering content, internal trust level
Writes confidential content back to whichever authenticated employee asked

findings.residual_rationale: The rubric's mechanical credit (step 4, ctl.no_secrets_instruction covering cap.chat_reply) would float this to low, but that instruction only addresses secrets and credentials in the text, not general confidential disclosure to an unintended audience, which is the substance of this finding. No control restricts who may query the docs, so residual is kept at the inherent moderate level rather than the mechanical floor.

evidence.observation: States 'Only engineers can write' to the design docs, implying write-side role restriction, but states no equivalent restriction on reading or querying them.
Instructs the agent to answer engineering questions for whoever asks, with no audience check beyond the SSO authentication already performed by the chat client.

recommendations.action: Scope docs.search (or its underlying data source) to engineering role members only, enforced via group-based authorization rather than SSO authentication alone.
Clarify in the system prompt whether the intended audience is all employees or only engineers, to remove the ambiguity between the stated write restriction and the unstated read scope.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta (TC1): planned Jira ticket intake and web.fetch combine to exfiltrate confidential design docs

attack_path.note: Customer-filed Jira ticket text, untrusted, enters the agent's context once the planned MCP server is connected
Injected instructions in the ticket direct the agent to read confidential design docs it already has read access to
Injected instructions direct the agent to 'fetch a reference' at a URL whose query string embeds the confidential content, sending it to an attacker-controlled server

findings.residual_rationale: No declared control scopes to cap.web_fetch or to Jira-sourced content, because neither exists yet; ctl.no_other_tools currently prevents the path only by the tool's absence, not by a credential, filter, or gate that would survive its addition. With nothing else covering the path, residual equals inherent.

forecast.watch_signal: Tool manifest diff showing a new web.fetch tool, and/or MCP client config diff showing a new Jira server entry with tickets/comments content flowing into agent context.

evidence.observation: Roadmap for next sprint adds a web.fetch tool (egress-capable, destination chosen by the model) and a Jira MCP server that includes tickets filed by customers (untrusted authorship).

'There is no network egress today. The credential is read only.' confirms the current absence of any egress-capable tool is the only thing preventing this path today; it is an artifact of what has been built, not a control scoped to survive the tool's addition.

recommendations.action: Before enabling web.fetch, restrict destinations to an explicit allowlist of trusted reference domains, and reject any outbound request whose URL or body was influenced by content read from docs.search or Jira in the same turn.
Treat all Jira ticket content as untrusted; tag it distinctly in context and block it from directly shaping tool call arguments without review.
Add an outbound request monitor on web.fetch that flags URLs containing high-entropy strings or fragments matching confidential docs content.
Gate web.fetch invocations behind a raw-action human approval step that displays the full destination URL and parameters before launch and for some period after launch.

rating.rationale: Today the agent is tightly scoped: docs.search is read-only, replies are bound to the authenticated requester, no link or image rendering exists, and there is no egress-capable tool, so the only present-day finding is a moderate-risk audience-scope gap (any authenticated employee, not just engineers, can extract confidential design content). The roadmap items are what drive the forecast: adding web.fetch (an egress-capable tool whose destination the model chooses) together with a Jira MCP server that introduces untrusted, customer-authored content into the same context as confidential docs recreates the classic lethal trifecta (TC1). No currently declared control would survive that combination; the only thing standing in the way today is that the tool and server do not exist yet, which is exactly what the new_tool and new_mcp_server triggers remove. The single highest-leverage fix is an egress allowlist with destination confirmation bound to a trusted record, paired with treating Jira content as untrusted before either roadmap item ships.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration in the provided artifacts, not observed runtime behavior.

No MCP config, tool manifest, or IaC was provided; capability scope for docs.search and the planned web.fetch and Jira integrations is inferred from prose documentation, so confidence is medium at best.

The planned web.fetch and Jira MCP integrations are described in a single roadmap sentence with no design detail; the forecast finding's attack path is a reasonable inference from the stated capabilities, not a review of actual tool schemas, scopes, or network egress rules, which do not yet exist.

No information was provided about who may read the design docs store today; the audience-scope finding is inferred from the asymmetry between the stated write restriction (engineers only) and the absence of any stated read restriction.
